original_value:
AbstractRuns‐rules have been widely used since the 1950s in industrial and nonindustrial process monitoring applications to improve the performance of basic and other traditional monitoring schemes. However, none of the studies on runs‐rules have accounted for a process with a combined effect of measurement errors and autocorrelation. Hence, in this paper, the use of the w‐of‐w runs‐rules to improve the performance of the Shewhart 
 scheme using an additive model with a constant variance and a first‐order autoregressive model is proposed. To reduce the combined negative effect of measurement errors and autocorrelation, we implement a sampling strategy based on rational subgroups in which (a) multiple measurements per item are taken (instead of a standard single measurement) and (b) non‐neighboring observations are gathered. Moreover, the latter sampling strategy is incorporated into the values of probability elements of a Markov chain matrix which is used to derive some closed‐form expressions for the zero‐ and steady‐state run‐length distribution. The main finding of this study is that, with respect to some overall performance measures, the proposed scheme outperforms the existing Shewhart 
 scheme by a significant margin. A real‐life example is used to illustrate the practical implementation of the proposed scheme.

result.paraphrase: Runs-rules have been widely applied since the 1950s in industrial and nonindustrial process monitoring to enhance the performance of basic and other traditional monitoring schemes. However, prior runs-rules studies have not considered processes affected jointly by measurement errors and autocorrelation. In this paper, we therefore propose using w-of-w runs-rules to improve the Shewhart scheme under an additive model with constant variance and a first-order autoregressive model. To lessen the combined adverse impact of measurement errors and autocorrelation, we adopt a rational-subgroup sampling strategy that (a) takes multiple measurements per item rather than a single standard measurement and (b) collects non-neighboring observations. In addition, this sampling strategy is built into the probability components of a Markov chain matrix used to derive closed-form expressions for the zero-state and steady-state run-length distributions. The key result is that, on several overall performance measures, the proposed scheme significantly outperforms the existing Shewhart scheme. A real-world example demonstrates how the proposed scheme can be implemented in practice.
